title: "A view added to an NSStackView while hidden never gets the stack's width alignment"
date: 2026-09-20
category: ui-bugs
module: RcGitApp
problem_type: ui_bug
component: frontend
symptoms:
  - "The Changes section in the sidebar is narrower than the sidebar and sits against its right edge"
  - "The narrow width tracks the content: an empty repository shows a ~147pt column, one with long stash messages a ~221pt one"
  - "The ref list above it fills the sidebar normally"
  - "No unsatisfiable-constraint log: nothing is broken, a constraint was simply never made"
root_cause: api_misuse
resolution_type: code_fix
severity: medium
framework_version: macos 26.6.2
related_components: [appkit, autolayout, nsstackview]
tags: [appkit, nsstackview, autolayout, detacheshiddenviews, alignment, width, sidebar, hidden-at-attach]

runs.text: A view added to an NSStackView while hidden never gets the stack's width alignment
stacks the mode's section under the ref list and swaps sections with
, so every arranged view is meant to be as wide as the stack.

The Changes section was not. It rendered as a narrow column pinned to the sidebar's right edge, its width set by whatever its widest row happened to need — the Apply/Pop/Drop row in a repository with no stashes, the "1 of 1 selected · Stash · Commit" row in one with a modified file. The ref list above it, which is never hidden, filled the sidebar correctly.
hid each section before handing it to the stack:
, a hidden arranged view is not in the view hierarchy, so the stack never laid the section out and never created its

alignment constraint. Unhiding the section re-attaches it but does not make the stack create that constraint afterwards. The section had no width constraint at all, so Auto Layout sized it to its content's own minimum.
The sidebar's Changes section is much narrower than the sidebar and hugs its trailing edge; the 8pt gutter is correct on the right and enormous on the left.
Its width changes with the content rather than with the sidebar: the same window shows a different gap in two repositories.
The ref list above the section is full width.
Console is silent. The layout is satisfiable — one constraint was never created.
A standalone AppKit probe reproduces it in three cases against a 253pt stack, with the pane sized by a 75pt button row:

rows.text: Added visible, then hidden, then shown
Added visible, hidden before any layout, then shown

runs.text: So it is not "hidden at some point" that loses the width — it is never having been laid out while attached. Hiding a view that the stack has already laid out is safe; a view that is hidden before the stack's first layout pass never receives an alignment constraint, and the stack does not backfill one when the view returns.
Give every view showing its width on every show, from
. The section is not the only view at risk: a window that opens on Files hides the ref list before the stack's first layout too. Since this fix the layout has moved the sections under
, which stands in for the ref list beside a section, so the ref list toggles as well:

The constraints are re-made rather than kept because AppKit drops an ancestor's constraints for a view it detaches, and hiding a view detaches it. Unhiding re-attaches the view synchronously, so the constraints can be activated in the same pass.

does the same for every row that toggles — the scan-truncation note, which is hidden before its stack is built, and the stash group, which is hidden in a repository with no stashes. A row that toggles goes through that helper; a row that is always there takes its width from the stack.
Hiding a view before the stack's first layout is allowed, but a view hidden, or added hidden, before an
first lays it out gets no
alignment constraint. The code that shows it must re-make its width on every show; never assume an unhide restores the stack's alignment constraints (
, the bullet "A view the stack has never laid out while attached").

Sizing that depends on content when it should depend on the container is the tell: measure the frame in a probe before reaching for hugging and compression priorities, which cannot fix a constraint that does not exist.
